latest_findings.claim: With data_seed 1, both fresh seeds reproduce the late-forming, late-strengthening force code seen on data_seed 0 (4 layers, d_model=128, N=64, e<=0.5, 5000 steps, best-of-5 controls). Final force margins are 0.187 (seed 79, R2 0.809 vs control 0.623) and 0.208 (seed 80, R2 0.817 vs control 0.608). Persistent force formation comes at steps 400 and 350, against step 100 for accel_step in both seeds, a lag of 300 and 250 steps. From step 500 to 5000, force gains +0.074 and +0.081 while accel_step gains only +0.025 and +0.022. accel_step still has the larger raw margin (0.165 and 0.191; R2 0.974 vs control 0.809, and 0.960 vs 0.769) and the larger headroom-normalised margin (0.86 and 0.83, vs 0.49 and 0.53 for force).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both seeds finished all 5000 steps and pass every expected-if-true criterion by a clear margin, so the pattern does not depend on the dataset. On this data_seed the force margins are slightly lower than on data_seed 0 (0.187-0.208 vs 0.21-0.23). Persistent formation steps were read from the trajectory with a strict >= 0.1 bar, and here they match probes_final.formed_at_step. Force control_spread is 0.027-0.028, so the bar stays at 0.1. Four limits apply. (1) Force has not been residualised against distance or accel_step. Its late gain runs alongside the fall in val_mse_ratio (about 0.27-0.41 at step 500 to 0.005-0.006 at step 5000), so it could be a sharpening read of the distance or accel_step code rather than a separate m2-weighted force feature. (2) The layer carrying force is not stable: in seed 79 the best layer moves from 4 to 1 at step 400 and back to 4 at step 2000, while seed 80 stays at layer 4 throughout. (3) Only two data_seeds have been tested. (4) Random controls at d_model=128 are high (0.61-0.62 for force, 0.76-0.81 for accel_step and distance), which squeezes the raw margins. What would change the verdict: if the force margin drops below 0.1 once accel_step and distance are regressed out of the force target, the late force code is a derived read rather than a force representation.

latest_findings.claim: At N=128 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the final force margin is in between the other arms in both seeds: 0.150 (seed 20, R2 0.642 vs control 0.492, layer 1) and 0.131 (seed 21, R2 0.603 vs 0.472, layer 1). That is below N=64 (0.21-0.26) and above N=256 (0.03-0.04), so force falls by roughly 0.1 per doubling of N, a gradual decline in log N. accel_step margins are 0.151/0.163 (R2 0.934/0.920 at layer 4, controls 0.783/0.757), with headroom-normalized margins of 0.70/0.67. The accel_step control did not fall from its N=64 level (0.77-0.79), and seed 20's 0.783 is just outside the predicted [0.66, 0.78] band.
latest_findings.confidence_note: The main force prediction holds in both seeds: final margins of 0.150 and 0.131 sit inside [0.08, 0.19] and clear of both falsifying bands. Normalized accel_step (0.70/0.67) is inside [0.62, 0.77]. The verdict is not 'supported' because one stated criterion fails narrowly: seed 20's accel_step control R2 is 0.7826, above the 0.78 upper bound. The hypothesis's mechanism also fails. It said the accel_step control would fall between N=64 and N=256 alongside force, but at N=128 the control (0.757-0.783) matches N=64, while force has already lost about 0.1 of margin. The force decline therefore does not move with the accel_step control. The force control (0.47-0.49) is also flat against N=64 (0.48-0.51) and N=256 (~0.5). Both runs are complete (3000/3000 steps) and beat the baseline (val_mse_ratio 0.069-0.071). Force had not levelled off at step 3000: it gained +0.006 (seed 20) and +0.004 (seed 21) over the last 500 steps. The N=128 value may therefore partly reflect slower force growth rather than a lower ceiling, and longer training could move it toward the N=64 band. Formation steps read from the trajectories match formed_at_step (force persistent from 1000 in seed 20 and 1500 in seed 21; accel_step from 500 in both). Seed 21's force best layer switched from 4 to 1 only at step 3000. Each arm has only 2 seeds and one data_seed. The verdict would become 'supported' if the band were judged at 2-decimal precision. It would become 'refuted' for the mechanism if added seeds kept the N=128 accel_step control at N=64 levels.

latest_findings.claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5), the final layer-1 force margin is 0.247 for seed 22 (R2 0.697 vs control 0.450, spread 0.003) and 0.234 for seed 23 (R2 0.684 vs control 0.450, spread 0.041). Both are >= 0.23, which puts N=64 at the N=16 level (0.236-0.275) and far above N=256 (0.033-0.040). With seeds 20/21 (0.215/0.261), the four N=64 seeds average about 0.239, so the force collapse lies between N=64 and N=256 rather than declining gradually. The flat-accel_step part of the hypothesis held: the layer-4 accel_step margin is 0.207 for seed 22 (R2 0.902 vs control 0.694) and 0.186 for seed 23 (R2 0.922 vs control 0.736). Headroom-normalized, that is 0.68 and 0.70, inside the predicted [0.62, 0.77] band and matching N=16 (0.68-0.69). Force leads accel_step on raw margin but trails it on normalized margin (0.45/0.43).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps, and both seeds meet the pre-registered expected-if-false force criterion, so seeds agree. Several things limit the result. (1) Seed 23 clears the 0.23 cut by only 0.004, and its force control spread (0.041) is the largest in this experiment. (2) Force is still rising at step 3000 in both seeds (about +0.009 to +0.012 per 500 steps), while accel_step has levelled off. The 'step vs gradual' reading therefore depends on comparing all N at a fixed 3000 steps, and growth rates could still differ by N. (3) Force peaks at layer 1, the same layer as distance (margin 0.70-0.71), so the force margin may be a nonlinear read of distance rather than an m2-weighted force code; no residualized probe exists yet. (4) Everything uses data_seed 0. (5) The 'refuted' verdict applies to the primary force prediction (gradual decline); the secondary flat-normalized-accel_step prediction was supported. The verdict would change if an N=128 arm landed midway (about 0.10-0.15), which would make the decline look gradual in log N, or if longer training let N=256 force catch up.

latest_findings.claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5, seeds 20-21), the final layer-1 force margin is 0.215 in seed 20 (R2 0.726 vs control 0.511), inside the predicted [0.07, 0.22] band, but 0.261 in seed 21 (R2 0.737 vs control 0.476). Seed 21's value is above the 0.23 cutoff and inside the N=16 range of 0.236-0.275, so the predicted monotonic drop in force with N is not shown. The accel_step half of the hypothesis holds in both seeds: layer-4 R2 is 0.935-0.938 against controls of 0.770-0.791 (raw margin 0.147-0.165), which gives a headroom-normalized margin of 0.70-0.72. That is inside [0.62, 0.77] and matches the N=16 and N=256 arms, while normalized force is lower at 0.44-0.50.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps (val_mse_ratio 0.0148-0.0149) and every margin clears its required_margin. Spreads are small for force (0.009-0.041) and accel_step (0.009-0.014). The verdict is inconclusive because the force prediction splits across seeds: one seed is just inside the band and the other is in N=16 territory. Taken together, the data look more like a step than a gradient: force at N=64 (0.21-0.26) is close to N=16 (0.24-0.28), and most of the drop to 0.03-0.04 happens between N=64 and N=256. The 0.047 seed-to-seed gap here is as large as the N=16 vs N=64 difference, so two seeds cannot fix where N=64 sits. Force is also still rising at step 3000 in both seeds (+0.006 to +0.008 per 500 steps), so the comparison depends on training length. The flat normalized accel_step result is consistent across seeds and with the other arms. Seeds 22-23 at N=64, plus an N=128 arm, would settle the shape of the force curve. If both new N=64 seeds land at 0.23 or above, the result would change to 'refuted (step)'. If both land at 0.22 or below, it would change to 'supported'.

latest_findings.claim: In both seeds, force beats its best-of-5 control at the end of training, forms well after accel_step, and keeps strengthening while accel_step levels off. Its gain from step 1000 to step 5000 falls short of the pre-registered >= 0.08 bar. (a) Final force margin is 0.232 (seed 73, R2 0.776 vs control 0.544) and 0.218 (seed 78, R2 0.709 vs 0.490), against a required 0.1. Final accel_step margin is 0.177 / 0.175 (R2 0.964 / 0.967 vs control 0.787 / 0.792). (b) Read from the trajectory, accel_step persistently forms at step 100 in both seeds. Force persistently forms at step 300-350 in seed 73 (the 300 checkpoint rounds to exactly 0.100) and step 350 in seed 78, a lag of 200-250 steps. (c) From step 1000 to 5000, force gains +0.078 (seed 73, 0.154 to 0.232) and +0.063 (seed 78, 0.155 to 0.218), both under the 0.08 bar. accel_step gains only +0.019 / +0.015 (<= 0.04, as predicted). Measured from step 500 instead, the force gains are +0.109 / +0.086, which reproduces seeds 74/75. Headroom-normalized, accel_step still leads force in both seeds (0.83 vs 0.51, 0.84 vs 0.43).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs finished all 5000 steps (no early stop). Neither branch fits. Both seeds meet (a) and (b) and the accel_step half of (c), but the force gain from step 1000 to 5000 misses 0.08: narrowly in seed 73 (0.078, which rounding cannot lift above 0.08), and clearly in seed 78 (0.063). This is the reverse of the pre-registered 'late strengthening without late formation' case: here force forms late, and its strengthening after step 1000 is real but smaller than predicted. Most of the late force gain happens between steps 500 and 1500 and then slows (about +0.004 to +0.012 per 500 steps after step 2000). The two seeds agree on every sub-criterion. The verdict is inconclusive because the outcome falls between the pre-registered branches, not because the seeds disagree. Three things limit interpretation. First, probes_final.formed_at_step for force is 400 in both seeds, while the trajectory shows persistent crossing at 300-350. This is another formed_at_step-vs-trajectory lag (cf. q-20261012-032843-df65), so formation is quoted from the trajectory. Second, from steps 700-750 onward, force's best layer moves from layer 4 to layer 1, the layer where distance peaks (distance margin 0.22-0.26, also still rising). So the late force gain may be a sharper 1/r^2 read of the distance code rather than an m2-weighted force. Without a residualized force target, these cannot be told apart. Third, data_seed is fixed at 0. What would change the verdict: a pre-registered window starting at step 500 would make this 'supported'. A residualized force target (distance and accel_step regressed out) that drops below 0.1 would reclassify the late gain as a distance proxy.
